newsitem.title: UK: Drug mega-mergers "may be approaching limit".
newsitem.headline: Drug mega-mergers "may be approaching limit".

text.p: The spate of mega-mergers among the world's pharmaceutical companies could be getting close to saturation point if the industry is to go on exploiting its products efficiently, an industry consultant said on Wednesday.

"Considerable evidence suggests that there is a limit to how concentrated the pharmaceutical industry can become while still efficiently exploiting its products," John Ansell, who runs his own consultancy, told IIR's Pharma Summit.
"The industry may now be approaching that limit."

He said the result of recent mergers and acquisitions had been for companies like Glaxo Wellcome Plc and Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc to concentrate on key therapeutic areas and set sales thresholds for new drugs.

He said the danger was that if the industry became dominated by huge players, drugs with sales of $100 or $200 million a year would "no longer be considered worthy of promotion, because they could not possibly make a significant contribution to the bottom line of any surviving company."

And he pointed to risks in deliberately concentrating on existing areas of therapeutic leadership, noting that both Glaxo's best-selling drug Zantac and Wellcome's number one product Zovirax had emerged in areas where neither company had a track record.

Ansell said mid-sized players and companies that avoid mergers stood to benefit from a "windfall" of products and therapeutic categories that the industry giants decide not to pursue because they are deemed "non-strategic."
And he said these companies would also find it increasingly easy to get rights to smaller products "as the mega-merged companies will be forced to concentrate increasingly on blockbusters."
